80805.subject: More Trading, Different Activity: Avalanche’s Latest 30 Days
80805.body:
View this post on the web at https://www.team1.blog/p/more-trading-different-activity-avalanches

Nansen recorded 48.4 million transactions, down 33% from the previous 30 days. At the same time, DEX volume climbed to $2.7 billion, up 145%, while active users increased 8.1% to 1.6 million.
So Avalanche was not simply quieter. There were fewer transactions in Nansen’s dataset, but much more trading volume. Users still grew, capital continued moving through the ecosystem, and activity across individual Avalanche L1s adds another part of the picture.
Trading picked up fast
The biggest change is DEX volume. WAVAX alone accounted for around $2.5 billion, with roughly $1.3 billion in buys and $1.3 billion in sells.
Active users also moved higher, reaching around 1.6 million, up 8.1% from the previous period. If that user growth continues while transactions stabilize, this month may end up looking more like a change in how Avalanche is being used than a simple drop in activity.
Want to keep up with the latest in the Avalanche ecosystem? Subscribe to the Team1 blog and get our updates in your inbox weekly.
AVAX and WAVAX are moving differently
Around $4.6 million of native AVAX left exchange wallets over the latest seven days. WAVAX went the other way. Around $12.3 million moved into exchanges, while Top PnL wallets reduced their WAVAX positions by roughly $2.2 million.
Native AVAX is moving away from exchanges while WAVAX is moving toward them. At the same time, WAVAX remains extremely active on DEXs. For now, it looks more like capital moving around the ecosystem than everyone taking the same position.
Fresh wallets are still bringing money in
Fresh wallets added approximately $20.8 million in AVAX over seven days. Another $16.3 million went into WAVAX. Those are meaningful inflows, but both were below their normal levels. AVAX was running at around 0.6x its average flow, while WAVAX was around 0.4x.
New wallets are participating, just not at an unusually high rate. There is fresh capital coming in, but this does not look like another sudden wave of adoption.
BTC.b is still doing real volume
BTC.b continues to be one of the more active parts of Avalanche DeFi. It recorded around $238.8 million in DEX volume over 30 days, with approximately $1.3 million in net flow.
Over the latest seven days, BTC.b generated another $60.9 million in volume, with $31.5 million in buys and $29.4 million in sells.
There is no major imbalance between buyers and sellers. It is simply an active market.
Bitcoin liquidity gives Avalanche another source of capital beyond AVAX and stablecoins, and BTC.b is still moving through the ecosystem rather than simply sitting in wallets.
sAVAX looks steady
sAVAX has around 16,609 holders, approximately $169.8 million in market cap, and roughly $2.2 million in liquidity. Seven-day volume was around $743,000, with approximately $424,000 in buys compared with $319,000 in sells.
There is no obvious new staking surge here.

80804.subject: JPMorgan shut AI Agents out of Chase. Mercury let them in, and AI Assistants now recommend it 5 to 1 😳🏦; Stripe …
80804.body:
View this post on the web at https://linas.substack.com/p/fintechpulse1138

Hey Everyone,
Good morning & happy Wednesday! Today, we’re breaking down JPMorgan Chase’s decision to block outside AI agents like Meta’s Muse from Chase accounts to see why the ban protects $2.7 trillion in cheap deposits but still leaks (what the block actually stops & what slips past it, what JPMorgan’s own Smart Cash agent says about the bank’s real motive here, and what to watch next + bonus deep dives into Revolut building its own AI agent [ https://substack.com/redirect/a1a827d3-7808-4268-8a17-894bea3971c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] & How to Hire a Grok Bot: Your First AI Employee [ https://substack.com/redirect/cb535944-9dd8-42ea-a7f5-de0b58b4ada9?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside), and diving into Stripe bringing its Privy wallets to the XRP Ledger to see what it tells us about who will own the wallet layer of agentic finance (what actually ships today vs. what was announced, how Stripe squares being “blockchain agnostic” with pushing its own Tempo chain & OUSD stablecoin, & what to watch next + bonus deep dive into Stripe [ https://substack.com/redirect/f953d231-dd46-4551-963a-75e2b04875ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], and a16z’s State of Markets 2026: The AI Playbook for Founders and Investors [ https://substack.com/redirect/f06e5da0-1d8a-4c9a-a9cb-86383e15622e?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] inside). So let’s just jump straight into the interesting stuff 🌶️
JPMorgan shut AI Agents out of Chase. Mercury let them in, and AI Assistants now recommend it 5 to 1 😳🏦
Following the Agents 🤖 Banking giant JPMorgan Chase $JPM  won’t let outside AI agents such as Meta’s Muse [ https://substack.com/redirect/c2ebbc59-dc9b-412f-8bb9-e0703eba8146?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ] log into customer accounts or move money, CEO Jamie Dimon said on Tuesday. The ban keeps agents out of Chase. It doesn’t stop them from talking customers into taking their money elsewhere, and that money is the cheapest funding JPMorgan has: $2.7 trillion in average deposits, with Chase Savings paying just 0.01% (which is incredibly low vs. what fintechs are offering).
Two weeks ago, in our Agentic Bank Run piece [ https://substack.com/redirect/2c6ffa90-a23b-4ff2-893e-449eeef6ed08?j=eyJ1IjoiMXN4Zm00In0.wehL2Vke0PUDz1PHD6ZKtcy1ufIoeqpblecCEEWPpqI ], we predicted that big banks would block unidentified agents, build their own, and sell access later. JPMorgan has now done the first two. FinTechs like Mercury went the other way. It lets agents connect through a hosted MCP server, and AI assistants already recommend it over Chase by more than five to one. Not too shabby!
Let’s take a closer look at this to see what the block stops and what slips past it, what JPMorgan’s own agent says about its motive, why Merc

80801.subject: 🪦 Anthropic kills git
80801.body:
----------
######           [Subscribe](https://academynews.genai.works/)   -    [Collaborate with us](https://utm.genai.works/r/cq9vsh4)


--------------------
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8776fa6e-e2d0-4aec-9648-1bed6de3a659/GenAI_Daily_Banner.jpg?t=1778687445)
Caption: 


----------

----------
**Welcome back!** Claude wrote so much code that Anthropic had to replace git, the tool GitHub runs on. Google now lets you put apps you vibe code on your own Android phone. Gemini 4 Argon finally reached the Gemini app. And a mystery model called Claude Fable 5.5 showed up on Microsoft's cloud.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Anthropic:** Why did Claude force Anthropic to ditch git?

* **Google:** Why Android phones are a lot more interesting now?

* **Gemini:** Are you finally trying the new hyped-up model?

* **Claude:** Where did Fable 5.5 pop up?


----------







----------
## Claude wrote so much code that Anthropic dumped git

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/86f75ca8-c864-44ab-a8fa-1e5998495aab/c671a3b1-a805-414c-8ac8-39d4cbe349dc.jpg?t=1791966971)
Caption: 

In May, Anthropic merged about 2,500 code changes a day. By September it was [merging more than 30,000 a day](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control), and it says Claude's coding caused the jump.

Git, the standard tool developers use to track code changes and the one GitHub is built on, couldn't keep up. So Anthropic replaced it for its own code.

Seven people built the replacement, called Scion, in five months. They also built their own code review tool.

* Anthropic's automated tests grab a copy of its code about 25 million times a day.

* At the peak, it ran several hundred copies of its git servers to keep up with the load.

* Scion runs on 200x less computing power, and code downloads take seconds instead of minutes.

* Every engineer on the team now rates Claude a better coder than themselves. A lot of their job became telling Claude no.

* One of the top replies on X came from someone whose single pull request has been stuck since March. It fixes a typo.

Anthropic isn't releasing Scion yet. It expects other companies to hit the same wall within a year and wants to help GitHub and GitLab bring the best parts to git.


----------





----------
## Build an AI agent and win big

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4efe859a-6ea4-46e5-bd7a-f69d08b86b05/7857fe58-83e4-411c-9d29-b1c0ef21cc88.png?t=1791921142)
Caption: 

Our Open Agent Hackathon runs online from October 22 to 27, for teams of one to five. Build an agent that does real work for a real person, then let the judges try to break it.
